form_analysis.feedback: Strong aftercare for a combined acid peel. Effectively communicates the unique aspects: rapid frosting, potential for significant peeling, and salicylic acid's systemic caution. Good balance of managing a medium-depth peel's recovery with specific ingredient warnings.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare protocol is for a Jessner's peel, a combination of salicylic acid, lactic acid, and resorcinol. It creates a rapid, even frost and is effective for acne, pigmentation, and photodamage. It is considered a medium-depth peel with a significant healing process.

instructions.general_directive: Follow the General Chemical Peel Principles and the Medium-Depth Peel Aftercare instructions. Jessner's-specific notes are below.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Symptoms and Timeline
sections.content: Rapid frosting (whitening) occurs within minutes. Significant redness, tightness, and a burning sensation for the first 24-48 hours. Swelling peaks on day 2. Skin darkens to a bronze/grey colour before peeling begins around day 3-4. Peeling is often pronounced and in large sheets over 4-7 days.

sections.title: Jessner's-Specific Care Points
items: Rapid Frost: The quick frosting is normal. Do not be alarmed.
Resorcinol Note: This component can cause a temporary grey/brown discolouration before peeling. This is not scarring.

Salicylic Acid Systemic Effect: In high doses or over large areas, salicylic acid can be absorbed systemically. Report any symptoms of salicylism to your practitioner immediately: ringing in the ears (tinnitus), dizziness, nausea, rapid breathing, or confusion. (This is rare with facial peels).
Aftercare Soaks: You will likely be instructed on a specific soaking/cleansing regimen to soothe the skin and facilitate peeling.

sections.title: Sun Protection and PIH Risk
sections.content: The skin is highly susceptible to pigmentation changes post-peel. Strict sun avoidance for 4-6 weeks is mandatory. Daily use of a physical sunscreen (SPF 30-50) begins once peeling is complete.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions (Strict)
items: No exercise, sweating, or heat exposure for 7-10 days.
Plan for 5-7 days of social downtime due to visible peeling.
Do not pick or pull the peeling skin.

sections.title: Complication Awareness
sections.content: Contact your practitioner immediately for: signs of infection (pus, increasing pain, fever), cold sore outbreak, symptoms of salicylism (see above), or any areas of intense, persistent pain or dark discolouration that does not peel.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: Do NOT apply makeup until all peeling is complete (typically Day 7-10).

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Itching is common during the peeling phase.
The new skin will be pink and smooth. Redness can persist for several weeks.
Jessner's is excellent for treating acne, melasma, and solar lentigines (sun spots).
A series of 3-6 peels spaced 3-4 weeks apart is typical for optimal results.

patient_declaration.reading_confirmation: It is essential that you have read all of the information available. Once you have read and understood all of the below, please sign the declaration at the bottom of this form.
patient_declaration.question_opportunity: Please let your practitioner know if you have any questions or if you do not understand any of the aftercare instructions provided below.
patient_declaration.declaration_text: I confirm that I have read and understood all the information on this Form. I am aware of the rare risk of salicylate toxicity and will report any concerning symptoms. I have been given the opportunity to ask any questions that have come to mind throughout.

recommendations: Ensure patients with aspirin allergies are identified pre-treatment, as salicylic acid is related.
